name: s42_00000.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and round. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center. On the left is a Sights Set sign, an upward arrow on a stem ending in a small diamond. On the right is a water sigil, an S-curve between two teardrops, drawn slightly roughly. Each is small, about a quarter of the ring's radius. A Projection sign, a flat-topped bracket, sits at the south-southeast with its top toward the center. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three short strokes, sits near the ring at the northeast with its top toward the center. A Holding sign, two curved strokes each with a dot, sits at the west, turned with its top toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size gives a modest intensity, and its slightly rough lines make the effect a little weaker and shorter lived. Sights Set at the center lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen point. Projection works with it to send the effect outward from the seal toward that point. Holding is likely non-directional, so its rotation does not change its effect. It keeps the water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. Aeriforms Defined is a poorly understood air modifier. It is read here as giving the water an airy, vapor-like character, which is a guess. Aiming and projection serve one purpose, so the seal combines three kinds of modifier and stays coherent. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no side is favored beyond where the caster aims.
effect: Sends a small, cohesive cloud of misty water outward toward a point the caster aims at. The cloud keeps its shape as it travels. It is fairly weak and thins out and disperses somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00001.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly round. A water sigil of moderate size sits at the center. Four smaller sub-seals sit inside the main ring. At the north-northwest is a neat, closed ring holding a Glaives sign at its center, with no sigil. At the east-northeast is a closed ring holding a small water sigil. At the south-southeast is a closed ring holding a wind sigil. At the west-southwest is a closed but heavily wobbly, lumpy ring holding a light sigil. Seven signs sit near the main ring. Three Crosshair signs are at the north, east-southeast, and south; the north one crosses the edge of the north-northwest sub-seal and the south one crosses the edge of the south-southeast sub-seal. A Convergence triangle at the east-northeast is drawn with a heavy, jagged outline that overlaps the water sub-seal's ring, and its point faces outward rather than inward. A Partition sign at the west faces inward. A Stillness sign sits at the northwest, and a Windows sign, a small hatched ring, sits at the southwest. Some strokes overlap, but every glyph is legible.
justification: The central water sigil sets the element, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. The water and wind sub-seals add their own water and moving air. The light sub-seal adds a glow, but its ring is far from round, so that part is fleeting and may fail to activate. The Glaives sub-seal has no sigil, so it acts only as a modifier, setting how deeply the magic embeds into flesh. The three Crosshair signs are the most numerous modifier, so targeting dominates: the effect is aimed at whatever their short ends point toward, on several sides. Partition outlines the borders of the area of effect. Convergence normally focuses magic to a single point, but here it points outward. Reading this as reversing the focus into a spreading effect is a guess, and it works against both the Partition boundary and the Crosshair targeting. Stillness holds magic in place, which contradicts the outward targeting and the moving air from the wind sub-seal. Windows links two spaces that are not physically connected. Together this stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier around the main sigil, with several pulling in opposite directions. The water sigil and the Crosshair targeting dominate, and the result is likely unstable. The roughness of the Convergence, Stillness, and Partition strokes, and of several sub-seal rings, weakens those parts further and shortens how long they last.
effect: Produces water that is pushed toward targets on several sides within a bounded area, carried on moving air and lit by a faint glow, and able to sink into the flesh of what it strikes. The effect is erratic: the water spreads unevenly instead of gathering, portions meant to hold still waver and slip loose, and the light sputters out almost at once or never appears. Some of the water may surface in an unconnected location, and the whole effect tends to collapse early.

name: s42_00002.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain white background, ring closed and drawn round and neat. A small light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short strokes reaching outward, sits at the center and is small relative to the ring. Near the ring at the north-northwest is a Partition sign, its peaked top toward the ring. It is small and its strokes are slightly uneven. Near the ring at the south-southwest is a four-lobed Billow sign, drawn cleanly. Both signs sit on the western half of the seal, and the eastern half is empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates light, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Light from this sigil diminishes over time. Billow is not at the center here, so it acts as a modifier rather than the core of the spell. It turns what the spell produces into a soft, fluffy, cloud-like mass, which gives the light a puffy, billowing form instead of a beam or point. Partition outlines the borders of an area of effect that extends outward and upward, so the cloud of light is held within a defined region. Its rough strokes slightly weaken that boundary. Both signs sit on the western side with nothing to balance them, so the effect leans west of the seal instead of centering over it. The two modifiers do not conflict, so the seal should hold together.
effect: Produces a modest, soft cloud of glowing light that puffs up within a bounded area offset to the west of the seal. The edge of that area is a little uneven and wavers on its northwest side. The glow dims gradually over time.

name: s42_00003.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Inside the inner ring, a Concealment sign (an eight-armed star with eye marks) sits at the southeast and an Envelopment sign (a slanted stroke with hooked ends) sits at the southwest. In the band between the two rings are five Crushing signs at the north, east-northeast, southeast, south, and west-northwest. Each is drawn with its top toward the center, so the northern one reads as a W and the southern one as an M; all five are inverted. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves and manipulates air, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Crushing is semi-directional, so inverting it reverses its effect: instead of breaking solids apart, the five inverted signs pull crushed or scattered material back into its original form. Five of them spread evenly around the outer band make that reforming strong and even on all sides. Concealment hides a target, and Envelopment makes an effect surround what it targets. Together they wrap the target in a hiding layer, as in shadow-cloaking seals. Read together, the air current carries loose fragments and dust, the inverted Crushing reassembles them, and Concealment with Envelopment shapes the result into a covering that hides whatever it surrounds. These modifiers work toward one purpose and do not contradict each other.
effect: Stirs a steady current of air that sweeps up nearby dust and broken fragments and temporarily fuses them back into solid pieces. Those pieces are wrapped around the target as a shell that hides it from view. When the spell ends, the reformed material crumbles back into loose debris.

name: s42_00004.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is open, with a gap at the lower right, and is drawn roughly and somewhat out of round. A small fire sigil sits at the center. Six identical signs are spaced evenly around it at about two thirds of the way to the ring, at the northeast, east, south-southeast, southwest, west and north-northwest. Each sign is a small octagon crossed by two lines. Rotation makes some crosses read as a plus and others as an X. The signs at the west and northeast are drawn heavier than the rest. Three smaller closed rings touch the main ring from outside. The rings at the northwest and east-northeast each hold a small light sigil, and the ring at the south holds an Immobility sign at its center.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The crossed octagon matches no known sign exactly. It is closest to Selection, a cross drawn through an enclosing shape, so reading it as Selection is a guess. Read that way, the six signs confine the spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. Because they are evenly spaced and non-directional, they push the effect in no particular direction. The two attached light sub-seals add light, which falls within the fire domain, so the heat also gives off a glow. The attached Immobility sub-seal keeps the target fixed in relation to the seal, so it holds its shape and position. The seal does not activate while the ring is open. The rough linework and the ring's uneven roundness would make any effect weaker and short-lived once the ring is closed.
effect: It does not activate as drawn. Once closed, it would make the object it is drawn on give off modest heat and a soft glow, with the effect held fixed in place and kept from spreading beyond that object. The warmth and light would flicker unevenly and die out sooner than a cleanly drawn version.

name: s42_00005.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and fairly round. Two small glyphs share the center side by side: a Strengthening sign on the left and a water sigil on the right, each roughly a fifth of the ring's radius. Four Crushing signs sit about two-thirds of the way out, one each at the north, east, south and west points, with their peaks facing the center. The north one reads as a W and the south one as an M, matching the inverted arrangement. The east Crushing sign is drawn a little roughly; the others are neat. A single Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks on four arms, sits near the ring at the southeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on water. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crushing is semi-directional, and all four are inverted, so instead of breaking matter apart they pull scattered material back into its original form. Here that is broken or scattered water, and the reformed shape lasts only while the spell holds. The Strengthening sign at the center makes the reformed water harder and more durable. The lone Concealment sign hides the target. Because it sits only at the southeast, the seal's signs are unbalanced and the hiding leans to that side. Strengthening, reforming and concealment are three compatible kinds of modifier and do not contradict each other. The slightly rough east Crushing sign weakens the reforming pull on that side a little.
effect: Draws scattered or splashed water back together into the shape it held before and firms it so it holds together more solidly, falling apart again once the spell ends. The effect is modest in strength. The reformed water is partly hidden from sight, but the concealment pools unevenly toward one side, and the pull is slightly weaker on the opposite side, so the water there gathers more slowly and loosely.

name: s42_00006.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The outer ring is closed but drawn as a lumpy, uneven loop that is far from round. A small, roughly drawn water sigil sits at the center. Three Dispersion signs sit at the west, north-northeast and south-southeast, each with its stem toward the center and its curve toward the ring. Two Glaives signs sit inside the ring: one at the west-northwest with its prongs toward the ring, and one at the east-northeast inverted, with its prongs toward the center. A Crushing sign at the south is drawn as a W, its points toward the ring. Three small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. At the southwest is a closed sub-seal holding a water sigil that fills about half of it. At the north is a closed sub-seal holding a Projection sign. At the east-southeast is a sub-seal whose ring is open, holding a small earth sigil. Most of the signs are drawn roughly.
justification: The central water sigil sets the element, but its small size gives low intensity. The large water sigil in the southwest sub-seal adds a stronger secondary source of water. The three Dispersion signs, evenly spaced, make the water pour outward in all directions rather than form a beam. Crushing breaks its target into smaller pieces. Acting on water, it most plausibly shatters the flow into fine droplets. The north sub-seal's Projection sign pushes the effect outward from the seal. The earth sub-seal's ring is open, so it contributes nothing until closed. The two Glaives directly contradict each other, one normal and one inverted, so their control over how deeply the magic embeds in flesh largely cancels and behaves unpredictably. The seal also stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: Dispersion, Glaives, Crushing and Projection. Dispersion and the water sigils dominate, but the result is likely unstable. The rough strokes make it weaker and shorter lived. The badly misshapen outer ring means the effect would be fleeting at best or might fail to activate.
effect: Sprays water outward from the seal in all directions as a fine, broken mist, with one side gushing noticeably harder than the rest. The spray sputters and wavers in strength, and wherever it reaches skin it sometimes soaks in deeply and sometimes barely touches. It collapses after only a moment, if it starts at all.

name: s42_00007.png
description: A fully visible seal in black line on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed. The outer ring is slightly rough. A small, neatly drawn water sigil sits at the center, roughly a fifth of the ring's radius. A large Reflection sign, an hourglass of two triangles, sits at the northeast against the inner ring. A small Glaives sign sits inside the inner ring at the north-northwest, its prongs pointing toward the center. Three Repetition signs sit in the band between the rings, at the north-northwest, the west-northwest and the south. The west-northwest one is drawn darker and heavier than the others. A Refuse sign straddles the inner ring at the west-southwest, its diamond end toward the center. A small Purification curl sits at the east-southeast, near the inner ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size gives low intensity, and the slightly rough outer ring weakens it a little more. Purification separates waste from water. Refuse points inward, so it draws that waste toward the center. These two signs work together as a cleansing core. The three Repetition signs are the most numerous modifier, so they dominate, and they keep resetting the water to the state it had when first affected. Together with the cleansing core, this holds the water clean. The second ring adds strength to that combined effect. Reflection is unrelated: it targets a reflected image on the surface the seal is drawn on, and its large size gives it real weight. Glaives is also unrelated: it sets how deeply magic embeds into flesh, though it is small and roughly drawn. This stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: cleansing, time-resetting, reflection and embedding. The water, Repetition and cleansing parts dominate, Reflection competes noticeably, and the result is likely unstable.
effect: Gently cleans a small amount of water, pulling impurities to the center and keeping resetting the water so it stays clear. The cleansing wavers and acts unevenly. At times it seems to work on the water's reflected surface rather than the water itself. Water touching skin may cling and seep in briefly before the effect lapses early.

name: s42_00009.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, ring closed. A wind sigil sits at the center and is fairly large, reaching about halfway to the ring. Four Convergence triangles surround it: three in the inner band at the north-northwest, northeast and southwest, each turned at a different angle, and a fourth just inside the ring at the northeast with its flat edge toward the ring and its point toward the center. Three Binding signs sit close to the ring at the north, southeast and west-southwest, each with its smaller arc toward the center. A Strengthening sign sits at the west-northwest, tilted with its top toward the center. A small Cooling sign sits at the east-southeast, rotated so its bar runs diagonally. A Partition sign sits at the south with its peak toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves and manipulates existing air, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Convergence focuses magic toward a single point and packs loose material tightly. With four of these, it is the dominant modifier, so the moving air is drawn together. The three Binding signs are the next strongest. They halt the gathered air and make it act as one unit. Strengthening adds hardness and durability, Cooling lowers temperature, and Partition outlines the borders of the area of effect. That makes five different kinds of modifier on one seal. The compacting signs (Convergence, Binding, Strengthening) work toward the same end and dominate. Cooling and Partition are single, unrelated additions that pull in other directions, so the result is likely unstable. The Convergence triangles are turned inconsistently, which further muddies how evenly the air is focused. The signs are balanced around the ring, so the effect has no favored direction.
effect: Draws the surrounding air inward and presses it into a dense, chilled mass that holds together as a single body inside a bounded area. The mass hardens unevenly and tends to waver at its edges. Its cooling and its boundary flicker in and out, so it may loosen and scatter back into ordinary air sooner than expected.

name: s42_00010.png
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but noticeably lumpy and uneven, bulging at the upper left and flattening along the right. A large Strengthening sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, a triangle crossed by a horizontal bar, drawn with thick, jagged strokes and spanning about half the ring's radius. Five Orb signs, each a small circle crossed by a slanted line, sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, and northwest. A single Crosshair sign, four short strokes around an empty center and slightly tilted, sits at the west. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Strengthening sign sets the spell's core behavior, which is making material harder, stronger, and more durable. Its large size relative to the ring gives that reinforcement fairly high intensity. The five Orb signs are non-directional and define a spherical space above the seal where material collects, filling from the bottom up under gravity. The Crosshair is directional and points the seal's effect at whatever its shorter ends face. The signs are spread evenly, so no side is favored. These three modifiers support each other rather than conflict. Because there is no element, the spell works on any material brought to it. However, the rough strokes weaken the seal and shorten its life, and the ring is far from round, which makes the effect fleeting and risks the seal failing to activate.
effect: Forms a spherical space above the seal where any material poured into it gathers from the bottom up and is hardened into a tougher, more durable mass, with the effect aimed at whatever the seal targets. The sphere's outline wavers and may not take hold at all. When it does, the hardening sets unevenly and fades after a short time.

name: s42_00011.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed. The ring is lumpy and noticeably out of round, wider at the upper left and flattened in places. A fire sigil sits at the center, small to moderate in size relative to the ring and a little roughly drawn. Two four-lobed Billow signs sit off-center at the east and west, both somewhat rough. Two neatly drawn Immobility signs sit near the ring, one at the north-northwest and one at the south-southeast, each with its crossbar toward the ring. A single Convergence triangle sits at the south-southwest near the ring, with a point turned inward and heavier, rougher strokes. The signs cluster unevenly, with more weight toward the south-southwest.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the seal creates and shapes flame or heat. Its modest size gives modest intensity. Billow turns material into a soft, fluffy cloud, and with two of them flanking the fire sigil, the flame takes a billowing, cloud-like form. The two Immobility signs make the target hold its shape and position relative to the seal. Convergence focuses magic toward a single point and packs loose particles tightly together, which directly opposes Billow's fluffy loosening. The two Billow signs outweigh the single Convergence, so the cloud form dominates, but the two pull against each other and the result is likely unstable. Because the signs are unbalanced toward the south-southwest, where Convergence sits, the effect leans to that side. The rough strokes and the poorly rounded ring make the spell weak and fleeting, and it may fail to activate at all.
effect: Raises a puffy cloud of flame that hangs fixed in place over the seal, keeping its shape as the seal moves. The cloud swells loosely but keeps clumping into a denser knot on one side, so it burns unevenly and lopsided. It flickers and collapses after only a brief moment, and it may sputter out without forming at all.

name: s42_00012.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings. The outer ring is open, broken along its left side. The inner ring, just inside it, is also open, with a gap at the upper left beside the north sign. A small Purification sign, a hooked curl, sits at the center in place of a sigil, at roughly a quarter of the ring's radius. Three Stretch signs are evenly spaced between the center and the inner ring, at the north, east-southeast and southwest. Each has its rounded side toward the center and its open end with flared feet facing out toward the ring. No element sigil and no other signs are present.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Purification sign is the core of the seal. Purification separates waste from water, so the spell works on water rather than calling up an element of its own. Its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Because Purification is asymmetric, its behavior is less predictable than symmetric signs. Stretch turns solid matter touched by the spell into long, flexible ribbons. Paired with Purification, it would act on the solid waste pulled out of the water rather than on the water itself. Stretch is not known to change when turned around, so drawing it rounded side inward is treated as its normal reading. The three Stretch signs are evenly spaced, so the effect favors no direction. The empty second ring adds no new modifier, but a doubled ring tends to strengthen the core magic slightly. Both rings are open, so the seal will not activate until they are closed.
effect: It does not activate as drawn. Once closed, it would separate dirt and waste from water passing over the seal and draw the separated solids out into long, flexible ribbons, leaving the water cleaner. The purifying is gentle in strength, and how thoroughly it sorts the waste may vary from one use to the next.

name: s42_00013.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and drawn neatly. A tall, narrow glyph sits at the center: a stretched triangle with a short stroke rising from each upper side and a stem below. It resembles a fire sigil drawn tall and reaches about half the ring's radius. Six small, identical unnamed glyphs sit evenly spaced along the inner ring, at roughly north, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, each with its top toward the center. Each looks like a Stillness sign with its right part missing. Those at the north, southeast, south-southwest and west-southwest are drawn a little roughly. A single Aeriforms Defined sign, three short strokes, sits inside the inner ring at the east, partway between the center and the ring, with its top toward the center.
justification: The central glyph matches no sigil exactly. Its closest match is the fire sigil, stretched tall, so it is read as a fire variant. This is a guess, and it would make the spell create flame or heat, likely drawn upward into a tall shape. Its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity, and the second ring adds strength to the core spell. The six edge glyphs are closest to Stillness, also a guess, and would hold the magic static in one place. Because they are evenly spaced, the hold is balanced on all sides rather than pushed in one direction. The roughly drawn ones weaken that hold slightly on their sides. Aeriforms Defined modifies a spell toward air and gases. Paired with fire, it would turn some of the heat into warm air. Its lone placement at the east gives that air a slight lean in that direction. The two kinds of modifier do not conflict.
effect: Raises a tall, fairly strong flame or column of heat that stays fixed in place above the seal, surrounded by a body of warm air that drifts slightly to one side. The hold is weaker toward the south and southwest, so warmth slowly leaks away unevenly there and the effect fades sooner than it otherwise would.

name: s42_00014.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background, ring closed. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center. On the left is a small, slightly rough glyph resembling the wind sigil: the spiral and its flanking dashes are present, but the lower part of the spiral is missing. On the right is a somewhat larger, neatly drawn glyph resembling the light sigil, a diamond set in a square with four arms crossing it. Its halves are mirror images of each other. Six signs are spread evenly around the seal. Two Entwining signs sit at the north-northwest and southwest with their tops toward the center. Three Orb signs sit at the northeast, west-northwest and south. At the east-southeast is a glyph resembling a Solidification sign stretched wide and set at an angle. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Neither central glyph matches a sigil exactly. The left one is closest to the wind sigil and the right one to the light sigil; both readings are guesses. The light glyph is larger and neater, so light dominates and sets the main element. The wind glyph is small, rough and incomplete, so its air-moving contribution is weak and short-lived. The three evenly spaced Orb signs define a spherical space above the seal where the spell's material collects, filling from the bottom up. The two Entwining signs make the effect wrap itself around other objects. The stretched glyph is read as Solidification, also a guess; stretched wide, it would make the magic firmer over a broader area. These three kinds of modifier do not contradict each other, and the signs are balanced, so the spell has no set direction.
effect: Gathers light into a firm, glowing sphere above the seal that can wrap itself around nearby objects. A faint stirring of air drifts the sphere about, but the movement is weak and patchy and dies out well before the light does. The light itself dims gradually over time.

name: s42_00016.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line on a white background. The ring is roughly drawn, lopsided rather than round, and open with a gap at the upper right. An earth sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring and drawn roughly. Six signs surround it. Two large, bold Strengthening signs sit at the northwest and southeast, each tilted at a different angle. Two Entwining signs sit at the northeast and southwest, tops toward the ring. A small Piercing sign at the east point lies nearly sideways. A small Coil sign at the west point lies on its side, top toward the ring. The signs are evenly spread around the seal.
justification: The earth sigil makes this a spell that works existing solid matter such as stone or soil, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. The single Piercing sign shapes that matter into a projectile, and one sign means one projectile. Strengthening makes the matter harder and more durable. Entwining makes it wrap around whatever it reaches. Coil softens physical matter, which directly contradicts Strengthening. The two large, bold Strengthening signs dominate the single small Coil sign, so the material should mostly harden. Combined with four different kinds of modifier, the result is likely unstable. The balanced placement adds no direction. The rough drawing makes the spell weaker and shorter lived, and the lopsided ring may make the effect fleeting or keep it from activating. The ring is open, so the seal does not activate as drawn.
effect: Does not activate as drawn. Once the ring is closed, it would pull nearby stone or soil into a single hardened projectile that wraps around whatever it strikes. Patches of the projectile would turn soft or crumble unevenly while the rest stayed hard. It would hold its shape only briefly before collapsing, and might fizzle out before it forms at all.

name: s42_00017.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is hand-drawn and slightly lopsided rather than perfectly round. A wind sigil sits at the center at moderate size, about a third of the ring's radius, drawn with somewhat shaky lines. Four Diamond signs stand about halfway out from the center at the northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast and south-southwest, each tilted at a different angle. Two Purification signs, small hooked curls, sit at the west-southwest and southeast, each with its top turned toward the center. Two small Dancing Puppets signs sit near the ring at the northwest and northeast. Most of the inner signs are drawn roughly, and the northeast Dancing Puppets sign is the neatest glyph on the seal.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves and manipulates air, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Paired with wind, Dancing Puppets lets objects be lifted and steered through the air. These two are small and sit near the ring instead of surrounding the sigil, so that control is limited and loosely guided. The four Diamond signs likely confine the spell to objects inside the container the seal is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected. Purification separates waste from what it acts on, so with a wind sigil it would draw dirt and impurities out of the moving air. It is asymmetric, though, and its behavior is less predictable. The seal combines only three kinds of modifier and none of them conflict, so it holds together. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no direction is favored. The rough strokes and the slightly uneven ring make the spell weaker and shorter lived than a neat version would be.
effect: Stirs the air inside the container the seal is drawn on so that the objects within float and tumble about without disturbing the container itself, while dust and grime are pulled out of the circulating air. The currents are gentle and sputter, so objects bob unevenly and sometimes drop. The cleaning works patchily, and the whole effect fades fairly quickly.

name: s42_00018.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but lumpy and noticeably out of round, bulging at the upper left and flattened along the right. A neat wind sigil, an S-spiral flanked by short dashes, sits at the center and is small to moderate relative to the ring. A Regions sign, an angled two-stroke chevron, sits near the ring at the east-northeast with its point toward the ring, so it points outward. Two Convergence triangles sit partway out, one at the north-northeast and one at the east-southeast, each with a point toward the center. Two very small Mimicry signs sit near the ring, one at the west-northwest, drawn sideways along the ring, and one at the south, drawn slightly rough. Most of the signs cluster on the eastern side, leaving the west and southwest nearly empty.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves air, and its modest size gives a moderate intensity. The two inward-pointing Convergence signs focus that air down toward a single point. The single outward-pointing Regions sign makes the magic manifest outside the ring on its side, so the focused air is released toward the east-northeast. The signs are unbalanced, with most weight on that side, which reinforces the lean in that direction. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target. No decorative sigil is present, so here it would make the moving air follow or copy a target's motion. Both Mimicry signs are tiny, and one is rough, so that imitation is weak. Direction, focus and imitation are compatible kinds of modifier and do not conflict. However, the out-of-round ring weakens the whole seal and makes its effect short-lived.
effect: Draws air into a tight, focused gust and sends it out from the seal toward one side, where it loosely follows the movements of its target. The tracking is faint and lags behind the target. The gust itself flickers and gives out after only a brief moment.

name: s42_00019.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn in black line. The ring is open, with a wide gap along the west side, and is slightly lumpy but close to round. A fire sigil sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Collection signs sit at the north and south points, each with its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing the center. A sideways Reflection sign sits at the east-northeast near the ring. A Projection sign, a bracket shape with its open side toward the ring, sits at the northeast between the sigil and the Reflection sign. A small Envelopment sign sits at the northwest. A Gathering sign at the west-southwest points inward toward the center. A small Pulling sign at the east-southeast has its arrow pointing inward. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. The two Collection signs face inward in their usual orientation and gather material above and around the seal. The inward-pointing Gathering sign actively draws in surrounding material, and the inward Pulling sign pulls it toward the seal. Because the Pulling sign is drawn small, that pull is weak. Together these three signs feed heat and flame into the spell. The Envelopment sign makes the effect surround its target. Reflection targets an image reflected on the surface the seal is drawn on, and Projection casts that image outward. The signs fall into three related groups: drawing in, enveloping, and reflecting and projecting. They do not contradict one another, and the even spacing gives no single direction. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: The spell does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it would draw nearby heat and flame into the seal and wrap them around its target at moderate strength. It would also cast outward a fiery image of whatever is reflected on the surface the seal is drawn on.
